headline: Seduta ampiamente positiva a Wall Street: Coherent Corp. +16,79% guida i rialzi
headline_en: Broadly positive session on Wall Street: Coherent Corp. +16.79% leads gainers

paragraphs: Nella seduta del 9 novembre 2026 l'S&P 500 ha chiuso con 422 societa' in rialzo, 78 in ribasso e 2 invariate, su 502 titoli monitorati. La variazione media dell'indice e' stata di +2,40%.

Settori con la variazione media migliore: Information Technology (+4,42%); Industrials (+3,52%); Communication Services (+2,48%). Settori piu' debolli: Consumer Staples (+1,11%); Energy (+1,16%); Real Estate (+1,42%).

In cima alla seduta: Coherent Corp. (COHR, +16,79%), dove Barron's riporta: «Coherent Corp. Company & People | COHR»; Monolithic Power Systems (MPWR, +16,60%), dove MarketWatch riporta: «MPWR | Monolithic Power Systems Inc. Profile»; Advanced Micro Devices (AMD, +13,26%). In fondo: First Solar (FSLR, -4,74%), dove Barron's riporta: «First Solar Stock Is the Worst in the S&P 500 Today. U.S. stocks climbed on November 9, 2026, as investors regained confidence despite a series of headwinds that might have derailed sentiment. Oil fell as U.S.-Iran conflict risks eased, according to the Wall Street Journal, extending a retreat in oil futures on Middle East peace hopes. The session also saw Democrats investigating corporate America's biggest names, yet the market brushed off both the election aftermath and even a significant scandal involving Nvidia to continue buying stocks. The broad advance reflected this resilience: 434 stocks rose against 81 declines across 517 tracked issues, with an average gain of 2.45 percent.

Technology stocks led the session, with Information Technology and Technology sectors posting average gains of 4.42 percent and 3.79 percent respectively, while Industrials added 3.62 percent. The Nasdaq-100 outperformed, rising 3.46 percent on average with 86 stocks up and 15 down, compared to the S&P 500's 2.4 percent average gain on 422 up and 78 down. Coherent Corp. surged 16.79 percent, while Monolithic Power Systems gained 16.6 percent and Astera Labs climbed 13.72 percent. Advanced Micro Devices rose 13.26 percent; tracked outlets reported no specific company catalyst for that session. Teradyne advanced 12.73 percent after declaring a quarterly cash dividend, according to Financial Times. Applied Materials gained 11.37 percent, Bloom Energy added 11.91 percent, Flex Ltd. rose 12.02 percent with no reported catalyst, Ferguson Enterprises climbed 11.22 percent following its third-quarter earnings announcement, and Rocket Lab gained 10.91 percent.

Losers were concentrated in technology and healthcare, though declines were modest relative to the broad advance. Nvidia fell 4.27 percent after a short seller claimed the chip maker was involved in helping China access chips through undisclosed channels, according to MarketWatch. First Solar dropped 4.74 percent, with Barron's questioning whether blue wave optimism had been premature. Take-Two Interactive declined 3.48 percent despite lifting its annual revenue and profit forecasts as the GTA VI launch nears, according to Reuters. Thomson Reuters fell 3.79 percent with no reported catalyst, Akamai Technologies slid 3.37 percent after Jim Cramer expressed a preference for Cloudflare, and Axon Enterprise, PDD Holdings, DaVita, MicroStrategy, and Hershey Company each fell between 2.59 and 3.14 percent with no tracked catalysts. The Dow Jones, meanwhile, lagged with an average gain of 1.75 percent on 25 up and 4 down, reflecting weakness in large-cap industrials and financials relative to the tech-driven rally.
